issues.legal_issue: Whether payment of part of the agreed sale price was established despite evidence that differed from the pleaded account.
material_facts: The purchasers pleaded that they paid part of the sale price when the deed was registered, but their witnesses testified that payment occurred earlier at a residence.
The sale deed recited that part of the price had been paid, but there was no separate receipt or endorsement by the registering officer confirming payment.
The first appellate court considered the oral and documentary evidence, including the failure to call two alleged witnesses to the payment, and found that no part of the price had been paid.
The High Court affirmed that factual finding, and the purchasers challenged it in a civil appeal by special leave.
issues.conclusion: The finding that the purchasers had not proved payment of any part of the sale price did not warrant interference.
issues.legal_principle: A party cannot rely on evidence contrary to its pleadings; where the evidence departs from the pleaded case, the contrary evidence cannot establish that case. A factual finding reached after consideration of the evidence and affirmed by the High Court is not to be disturbed in an appeal under Article 136 of the Constitution without a valid ground for interference.

rule.if: civil_special_leave_appeal and evidence_contradicts_pleadings and fact_finding_considers_the_record and no_valid_ground_to_interfere

predicates.civil_special_leave_appeal: The proceeding is a civil appeal by special leave challenging a factual finding.
predicates.evidence_contradicts_pleadings: The evidence about when or how payment occurred differs from the account pleaded by the party asserting payment.
predicates.fact_finding_considers_the_record: The lower appellate court assessed the oral and documentary evidence before finding whether payment was proved.
predicates.no_valid_ground_to_interfere: No valid basis is shown for disturbing the lower appellate court's factual finding.
predicates.part_payment_not_established: The party asserting payment has not proved that any part of the price was paid.

issues.definition: When a civil special-leave appeal challenges a record-based finding of payment, evidence that contradicts the pleadings and no valid ground to interfere leave part payment unestablished.

issues.legal_issue: Whether title passes on execution and registration of a sale deed when the parties intend transfer to occur only upon exchange of the sale price and the registration receipt.
material_facts: The sale deed recited that the full price had been paid and possession delivered, but the purchasers did not prove payment of any part of the price.
The vendor retained the registration receipt pending exchange for the sale price, and possession was not delivered to the purchasers.
The parties' transaction was governed by the established practice of exchanging equivalents, under which title and possession were to pass upon payment and exchange of the registration receipt.
The purchasers did not tender the full price before the vendor repudiated the sale.
issues.conclusion: Title did not pass to the purchasers upon execution and registration of the sale deed because the parties intended title to pass only upon payment and exchange of equivalents.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 8 and 54 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, ownership ordinarily passes on execution and registration of a sale deed, but the parties' contrary intention, if expressed or necessarily implied, governs. Section 54 defines a sale as a transfer for a price paid, promised, or partly paid and partly promised. The intention is primarily gathered from the deed and, where its recitals are insufficient or ambiguous, from surrounding circumstances and conduct, subject to Section 92 of the Evidence Act, 1872. Bishundeo Narain Rai v. Anmol Devi and Kaliaperumal v. Rajagopal recognize that title need not pass on registration if the parties intended payment to be a condition precedent. The established practice of ta khubzul badlain likewise postpones transfer until exchange of the consideration and registration receipt where that was the parties' intention.

rule.if: registered_sale_deed and exchange_practice_applies and consideration_unpaid and registration_receipt_retained_pending_payment and possession_not_delivered

predicates.registered_sale_deed: The parties executed and registered a deed purporting to convey the property.
predicates.exchange_practice_applies: The transaction was governed by an established practice under which transfer was to occur upon exchange of payment and the registration receipt.
predicates.consideration_unpaid: The purchaser had not paid the agreed consideration when transfer was disputed.
predicates.registration_receipt_retained_pending_pa: The vendor kept the registration receipt to exchange it for the unpaid consideration.
predicates.possession_not_delivered: The vendor did not deliver possession to the purchaser as the deed recited.
predicates.title_not_passed_to_purchaser: Ownership did not pass to the purchaser upon execution and registration of the deed.

issues.definition: When a registered sale deed is subject to an applicable exchange practice and the consideration remains unpaid while the vendor retains the registration receipt and possession, title has not passed to the purchaser.

issues.legal_issue: Whether a vendor may repudiate a sale and convey the property to another purchaser when title has not passed and the agreed consideration remains unpaid.
material_facts: The vendor retained the registration receipt and possession because the sale price had not been paid.
The purchasers did not tender the full price before the vendor repudiated the sale.
The vendor repudiated the sale and subsequently conveyed the property to another purchaser, to whom possession was delivered.
issues.conclusion: The vendor was justified in repudiating the sale for non-payment, and the subsequent sale was valid.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 54 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, payment of the entire price is not ordinarily a condition precedent to a completed sale; if title has passed, the vendor's remedy for unpaid price is generally to sue for it and the vendor may have a charge under Section 55(4)(b). But the parties' intention determines whether title passed. Where the parties intended title to pass only upon payment and exchange of equivalents, the transaction remains uncompleted until that exchange, and the vendor may repudiate for non-payment. Bishundeo Narain Rai v. Anmol Devi and Kaliaperumal v. Rajagopal support these principles; the judgment also relies on the Patna High Court decisions recognizing ta khubzul badlain.

rule.if: title_not_passed_to_purchaser and consideration_unpaid and no_full_price_tender_before_repudiation and vendor_repudiated_before_resale and vendor_conveyed_to_later_purchaser

predicates.title_not_passed_to_purchaser: The purchaser did not acquire title under the earlier deed because the parties intended transfer to await payment and exchange.
predicates.consideration_unpaid: The agreed price remained unpaid when the vendor repudiated the transaction.
predicates.no_full_price_tender_before_repudiation: The purchaser did not offer the entire agreed price before the vendor repudiated the transaction.
predicates.vendor_repudiated_before_resale: The vendor repudiated the earlier transaction before conveying the property again.
predicates.vendor_conveyed_to_later_purchaser: The vendor subsequently transferred the property to another purchaser.
predicates.repudiation_and_later_sale_valid: The vendor's repudiation and subsequent conveyance are legally effective.

issues.definition: If title has not passed, the price remains unpaid, the purchaser has not tendered it before repudiation, and the vendor repudiates before reselling, the repudiation and later sale are valid.

issues.legal_issue: Whether a purchaser may obtain specific performance after the vendor lawfully repudiates a sale that was conditional on payment of the full price.
material_facts: The purchasers sought delivery of the registration receipt or original deed upon payment of the asserted remaining balance.
The courts found that the purchasers had not proved payment of any part of the price and had not tendered the full price before the vendor repudiated the sale.
The vendor repudiated the sale before the purchasers established that title had passed.
issues.conclusion: The purchasers were not entitled to claim performance of the sale.
issues.legal_principle: Where the parties intended that title would pass only after payment of the full sale price and the exchange of equivalents, the registered deed remains an agreement to be performed until that exchange. A purchaser who fails to tender the full price before lawful repudiation cannot claim performance on the basis of an offer to pay only part of the price. The principle follows from Sections 8 and 54 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, and the rules on intention and exchange of equivalents explained in Bishundeo Narain Rai v. Anmol Devi and Kaliaperumal v. Rajagopal.

rule.if: suit_for_specific_performance and title_not_passed_to_purchaser and no_full_price_tender_before_repudiation and vendor_lawfully_repudiated

predicates.suit_for_specific_performance: The proceeding seeks to compel completion of a sale transaction.
predicates.title_not_passed_to_purchaser: The purchaser did not acquire title because the parties intended transfer to await the required exchange.
predicates.no_full_price_tender_before_repudiation: The purchaser did not tender the full agreed price before the vendor repudiated the transaction.
predicates.vendor_lawfully_repudiated: The vendor repudiated the transaction when the agreed conditions for transfer had not been fulfilled.
predicates.specific_performance_unavailable: The purchaser is not entitled to compel performance of the sale.

issues.definition: A purchaser seeking performance cannot obtain it when title was to pass only upon the required exchange and the purchaser did not tender the full price before the vendor's lawful repudiation.
